Lotka–Volterra invariant and positivity Compare a positive orbit against an independently integrated log-coordinate reference. Assumptions, units and boundaries Use the dimensionless predator–prey equations x′=x(1−y), y′=y(x−1), initial state (1.2,0.8) and 0≤t≤20. Evaluate H=x−log x+y−log y only in the positive quadrant. Editorial clarification This is a finite-time comparison for one initial state. The continuum closed orbit is not an attracting limit cycle. RK4 is not claimed to preserve H exactly, maintain positivity at arbitrary steps or guarantee long-time geometric fidelity. Time, concentrations and populations do not define a spatial dimension. The rates are educational, not disease or experimental predictions. Adopted numerical method Integrate physical populations with classical RK4 at 400, 800 and 1600 fixed steps. Independent Radau/BDF references evolve log x and log y; the primary method uses neither a log-coordinate update nor invariant projection. x˙=x(1−y),y˙=y(x−1),(x(0),y(0))=(1.2,0.8),0≤t≤20x˙=x(1−y),y˙​=y(x−1),(x(0),y(0))=(1.2,0.8),0≤t≤20 H(x,y)=x−log⁡x+y−log⁡y,dHdt=0(x>0,y>0)H(x,y)=x−logx+y−logy,dtdH​=0(x>0,y>0) dlog⁡xdt=1−elog⁡y,dlog⁡ydt=elog⁡x−1dtdlogx​=1−elogy,dtdlogy​=elogx−1 References and measured quantities Measure state error against the independent reference, drift of H and the minimum saved population separately. The reference stage qualifies analytic Jacobians, Radau/BDF agreement, tolerance refinement and the identity dH/dt=0.
